revision.title: Nethermind: Formally Verified EVM for Ethereum
revision.summary: Nethermind will formally verify the complete Amsterdam EVM used in its zkVM guest, from Ethereum semantics through compiled .NET CIL to optimised RISC-V code. The proof will be reproducible and tied to the guest's exact build. Nethermind's regular Ethereum client shares EVM code with the guest; a published overlap manifest will identify which proved methods also appear unchanged in production builds. Adoption targets at least 20% of independently observed Ethereum execution-layer nodes running a release containing that shared implementation.

sections.why:
A zkVM proves that a guest program executed, but cannot establish that the guest implements Ethereum's rules correctly. An incorrect opcode, gas charge or state transition can produce a valid cryptographic proof of an invalid Ethereum result. The same implementation errors can affect ordinary execution clients.

This project will establish machine-checked correctness of Nethermind's Amsterdam zk-EVM, including its native RISC-V implementation, against an independent Lean specification. Nethermind's production EVM shares code with the guest. Publishing the exact verified overlap and measuring deployment of a release containing that code will show wider use, including validator infrastructure, RPC providers and personal nodes. Production-only branches and the regular client's native JIT code remain outside the proof.
sections.in_scope:
- Extend EVMYulLean to the complete Amsterdam EVM: opcodes, gas, nested calls, creation, memory, transient storage, state changes, reversions and exceptional outcomes.
- Extend LeanCIL to cover the zkVM interpreter's reachable CIL instructions and runtime operations, then prove the complete Amsterdam EVM-owned CIL implementation against that specification.
- Prove optimised RISC-V refinement for the zkVM EVM code using `il2rv64`, and compose the specification-to-CIL-to-RISC-V theorem.
- Verify precompile invocation, charging, inputs, outputs and failure behaviour against explicit external contracts.
- Publish reproducible proofs, build identities, coverage manifests and an independently checkable comparison of EVM methods in zkVM and regular Nethermind builds.
- Support public measurement of independent Ethereum execution nodes running a production release containing the documented shared EVM implementation.
sections.out_scope:
- Formal verification of the entire regular Nethermind EVM build or its .NET JIT-generated native code. Differing production CIL is not covered by the zkVM proof.
- Proofs of precompile internal algorithms, witness and SSZ processing, tries, complete block orchestration, zkVM provers or the full guest.
- Wider execution-client, consensus-client, L2-plugin and non-Ethereum verification.

Earlier Ethereum Foundation funding supported Cancun EVM/Yul formalisation; funding for this new scope is unconfirmed.
sections.why_grant: Nethermind has working but incomplete foundations. EVMYulLean models an earlier fork. LeanCIL verifies a supported subset of compiled CIL, not the full EVM, and its model targets .NET 10 while the guest builds with .NET 11. Funding must extend EVM-reachable CIL/runtime semantics and proof automation, align builds, and compose proofs. Existing ZisK, SP1 and OpenVM guests share `Nethermind.Evm` with the regular client under different configurations.
sections.commitments:
- Publish source and proof artifacts openly. LeanCIL uses MIT, EVMYulLean uses Apache-2.0, and `il2rv64` will use MIT.
- Nethermind will maintain the EVM proof integration and LeanCIL after the grant, updating proof coverage for future fork changes.
- Cover the complete Amsterdam zkVM EVM interpreter, including precompile invocation; publish all runtime and external-host assumptions.
- Attribute regular-client security benefits only to demonstrably shared, proof-covered methods; explicitly identify different or unproved production code.
- Count only independently operated, distinct, synced Ethereum mainnet execution nodes; exclude known Nethermind-operated infrastructure and duplicate observations.

milestones.name: Complete Amsterdam formal specification
criteria: Publish complete Amsterdam EVM semantics in Lean, including every opcode family, gas and precompile-call boundary; the independent reviewer checks the public coverage manifest.
Run Ethereum execution fixtures against the model in public CI; the reviewer reproduces the conformance report.

milestones.name: Verified zkVM EVM CIL
criteria: LeanCIL proves the complete Amsterdam zkVM EVM interpreter and its reachable EVM-owned CIL dependencies; the independent reviewer reproduces proofs against the hashed build manifest.
Public coverage checks reject unproved reachable EVM paths and modified build inputs; the reviewer reproduces the negative tests.

milestones.name: Verified zkVM RISC-V refinement
criteria: `il2rv64` checks RISC-V refinement certificates for the entire EVM-owned native-code closure; public CI binds certificates to CIL and machine-code hashes.
The independent reviewer reproduces the proof and rejection tests, and audits runtime, ABI, linker and precompile assumptions.

milestones.name: Composed correctness and shared-code evidence
criteria: Publish a Lean-checked Amsterdam-to-CIL-to-RISC-V correctness theorem for the full zkVM EVM interpreter; the independent reviewer reproduces it.

Publish a reproducible method-level CIL comparison between zkVM and regular-client builds, identifying identical proof-covered methods and excluded differences; the reviewer checks the manifest and release mapping.

milestones.name: Observable Ethereum execution-node adoption
criteria: At least 20% of independently observed, synced Ethereum mainnet execution-layer nodes run a release of Nethermind containing the documented proof-covered shared EVM methods; the independent reviewer checks public crawler records, version identities and exclusions of duplicate or Nethermind-operated nodes.
The reviewer independently verifies that counted production releases map to the published shared-method overlap manifest and zkVM proof artifacts, with every unproved production difference disclosed.

At least 2 proving operators independent of Nethermind publish proofs of Ethereum mainnet blocks made with the proof-covered Nethermind guest build for at least 30 consecutive days, confirmed by the technical reviewer
